correctness.rationale: Reconstructed exact graph definitions, f-vector 16/72/96/16, 88-pair acyclic matching with one critical vertex and 23 critical triangles, and 496 Hasse incidences. Proved 192 automorphisms by 16*12 upper bound from six-cycle and nine distinct two-neighbor signatures, matching 192 explicit affine maps. Computed signed invariant-face Lefschetz traces for all permutations, observed exact frequencies {-7:12,-3:4,-1:69,0:32,1:24,2:32,3:18,23:1}, and independently checked Fourier integrality of all 16 translation multiplicities. Finite group averaging gives invariants 2 for T and 0 for full group; rational exact coinvariants establish quotient homology. No extrapolation beyond finite enumerations is used.

originality.rationale: The published 23-sphere result is explicitly recognized as prior and contains no equivariant character. The new full 192-element character, 16 translation Fourier multiplicities, and distinct translation/full quotient invariants were checked against the prior full RESULT text, published graph-topology primary sources, and actual focused published-finding corpus and web searches. These are not logically determined by the old wedge homotopy type alone. Risk: undiscovered work could have an equivalent character.
residual_risks: An unindexed or unpublished equivalent equivariant computation may exist.
The character was checked computationally for one explicit finite graph; the result does not imply a uniform strongly regular graph theorem.

value.rationale: A canonical strongly regular graph has known 23-sphere independence-complex homotopy, leaving a natural genuinely unresolved equivariant question: how the full 192 graph symmetries permute and orient its independent two-sphere classes. The complete character and sixteen Fourier multiplicities classify this natural representation and show a concrete qualitative distinction: 2 rational degree-two classes survive T-orbits but none survive all symmetries. It is a motivated intrinsic invariant, not a random subgraph slice or a restatement of ordinary homotopy.
